British Values
British Values
British values are identified as:
At Bitham Brook Primary School we actively promote British Values, as defined under the Ofsted guidance 2014, through our school vision, curriculum and teaching: ‘… ensure that they and the school promote tolerance of and respect for people of all faiths (or those of no faith), cultures and lifestyles; and support and help, through their words, actions and influence within the school and more widely in the community, to prepare children and young people positively for life in modern Britain…’

pageCache.text:
Bitham Brook Primary School
About Our School
Our Vision
Our Vision
Our ethos is based on the school’s three core values, as chosen by the children and the wider school community:
‘In a community of kindness where all belong, be positive, be resilient, be creative’
Our vision is to provide all children with opportunities to flourish academically, personally, and socially and believe in their ability to succeed.
We want all children to:
The strength of character developed through academic, personal, and social experiences will empower children to increasingly participate in and contribute to their immediate and wider communities with confidence.
Staff, governors, pupils, and parents all have an important role to play in helping us to achieve our vision. The following identifies the ways in which our key stakeholders will contribute to the achievement of the school vision:
Provide inspiring experiences to nurture curious minds.
Vision Statement
'In a community of kindness where all belong: be positive, be resilient, be creative'
Our core values were chosen by the children of Bitham Brook Primary School in April 2022. These values reflect the behaviours that we hold dear; behaviours that will guide us to be a happy and successful community, and values that will help us to grow habits that will serve us well in life.
The Governing Body and parents were consulted on values chosen by the children and supported their choices. A strong theme in the parents' response was inclusivity and belonging. In light of this, belonging was added to our core values.

pageCache.text:
Bitham Brook Primary School
About Our School
Welcome
Bitham Brook Primary School is a vibrant and popular primary school in Westbury, with two-form entry across all year groups. As Westbury has grown in size, particularly on the east side of town in recent years, Bitham Brook has grown in numbers too. Our full extension was completed in Spring 2022, providing us with wonderful facilities to support and enrich the educational opportunities for children across the school. This includes a dance studio and a fully equipped design and technology room, in addition to a large hall for sports and gymnastics, a music and drama room and a beautiful and well-stocked library.
The building development work has enhanced the outside space available to our children here at Bitham Brook too, with a new multi-use games area (MUGA) and plenty of additional playground space being added without taking away any of our existing wonderful field space. With support from FOBBS, we have recently purchased new outdoor play equipment for all children, which is accessible throughout the year. We are also really proud of our allotments which are planted and cared for by our children as part of their outdoor learning.
For all the wonderful resources that we are grateful to have, our real riches come from the wonderful pupils and staff that make up our Bitham Brook community. We believe that every child deserves to have the best opportunities to learn, try new experiences and challenge themselves to be their very best. It is our pupils who have created our refreshed vision here at Bitham Brook, from characteristics they themselves find most important:
In a community of kindness where all belong: be positive, be resilient, be creative
The safety and well-being of our pupils is paramount, and by providing a culture of good order and discipline we can ensure a good and safe learning environment for our pupils to flourish. Our teaching sets high expectations which inspire, motivate and challenge pupils, which in turn promotes good progress. Adaptive teaching and the use of carousel groups enables teaching to respond to the strengths and needs of all pupils.
We hope that you enjoy your visit to our website, and that you find the information you are looking for. If you have any questions, please contact the school office and a member of the team will be pleased to assist you.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bitham Brook Primary School - Breakfast Club
pageCache.text:
Bitham Brook Primary School
Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club is run by school staff between 7.45 am and 8.45 am (term time only) and currently costs £4 per child per day for a 2 course breakfast. Breakfast Club booking forms are sent out via ParentMail towards the end of term for parents to book for the coming term. From these requests, the registers are created, places confirmed via email and payment requests issued. If you require any Breakfast Club spaces after the form deadline, please email admin@bithambrook.wilts.sch.uk to check availability.
Children can be dropped off for Breakfast Club at 07.45 or 08.00. If children are dropped off at any other time, please use the walkie talkie that will be in the foyer to contact the Breakfast Club team. Please remain with your child until they are met by a member of the Breakfast Club team (who will be with you as soon as possible).
We are able to accept childcare vouchers as payment, and Bitham Brook Primary is already registered with several providers. If you wish to pay using this scheme and can’t see our school listed, please email finance@bithambrook.wilts.sch.uk and we will be able to create an account for you to pay via this method.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bitham Brook Primary School - Adverse Weather Procedures
pageCache.text:
Bitham Brook Primary School
Adverse Weather Procedures
Adverse Weather Procedures
If we have adverse weather, we will make every effort to keep the school open, including gritting the paths on the school site. However, the safety of children and staff while at school and while travelling to and from school is of paramount importance.
If we decide to close the school, a message will be displayed prominently on the school website and we will send a text message to all parents who are registered with ParentMail and who have provided us with up to date mobile phone numbers.
The school telephone will be manned if at all possible.
School will be open if enough teachers and staff arrive to look after each class and if the essential infrastructure of the school (heating/lighting) is working. If it is impossible to supervise a class because not enough staff are present, the children in that class will have to be sent home.
In such an emergency situation we ask that no child be sent to school until it is certain that the class will be open. Please check the website and your phones for messages!

pageCache.pageTitle: Bitham Brook Primary School - After School Care
pageCache.text:
Bitham Brook Primary School
After School Care
After School Care
PH ActiveEd deliver fun and engaging After School Club at Bitham Brook for children of all ages.
On arrival, your child/ren will be offered a small healthy snack, such as a rice cake or piece of fruit before given the option to participate in a sports/games or arts and crafts activity. For those children who are booked on after 4:30 pm, a snack mid-session will also be provided e.g. sandwiches or wraps.
At PH ActiveEd's' Afterschool Club, children are provided with the opportunity of choice and the ability to access a variety of activities. Every activity is aimed to be accessible to children of all ages and abilities. Each session will run in a similar format where children will have the choice of 3 activities; craft, sports/games activity or choosing activities (lego, homework, books, board games etc.). There is also the option for some quiet time in the ‘chill-out zone’ which allows children who want a bit of quiet time to relax in an area where they can be comfortable.
Examples of sports activities include (not limited to): dodgeball, basketball, parachute games, tag games, alternative sports etc.
Costs (from Tuesday 22nd April 2025):
3:15 – 4:15pm: £6.30
4.00 - 5.45pm: £10.00
3:15 – 5:45pm: £12.90*
*includes a healthy, light snack
Be sure to follow all the instructions when registering (there is also a video tutorial on how to set up an account, click ‘Need Help Registering’ on the page in the above link). Once registered you will be able to log back in whenever you like to make your bookings.
We are OFSTED registered and therefore we are able to accept childcare vouchers as payment. If you are choosing to pay by childcare vouchers then please follow the link below for our carer details.
https://phactiveed.co.uk/pages/childcare-vouchers
If you have any questions regarding After School Club or any booking queries please email: bookings@phactiveed.co.uk

Bitham Brook Primary School
About Our School
Governors
Governors are responsible for school policy and make broad decisions about how the school is run.
The Headteacher is responsible for the day-to-day management of the school and carrying out agreed policies.
School governors have legal duties, powers and responsibilities. They can only act together, they cannot act individually. They meet at least twice a term at school and the minutes of meetings are available on request at the school for anyone to read.
Detailed information about the members of the Governing Body can be found here:
To contact the governors please email the Clerk to Governors at clerk@bithambrook.wilts.sch.uk or speak to the school office.
The Chair of Governors, Lucy Noble, can be contacted via clerk@bithambrook.wilts.sch.uk or c/o Bitham Brook Primary School, Arundell Close, Westbury, BA13 3UA.
